note: systemd units shipped into the image whose ExecStart names a program the build does not install. This file exists so that such a gap is recorded rather than discovered as a container-verification failure mixed in with environment noise. A unit not listed here whose program is absent fails repository validation.

gaps.finding: build/scripts/install-root.py copies systemd/ wholesale into /usr/lib/systemd/system, so the unit ships, but no step installs the program it starts. enterprise/policy.py is a library, not an executable.
gaps.impact: On an installed system the unit would fail to start. It is guarded by ConditionPathExists=/etc/bunny-os/enrolment.json, so it does not run on an unenrolled device, which is every device today: no enrolment has been performed and the enterprise pilot gate is BLOCKED.
gaps.notFixedHere: Writing the agent would be a new product feature. This pass is CI portability repair and hosted independent-build execution.

gaps.finding: scripts/bunny-brlapi-key.py exists and the unit ships, but build/scripts/install-root.py's script list omits it, so nothing installs the program. Surfaced by the installed-form unit verification when systemd 259.8 began refusing a non-executable ExecStart outright.
gaps.impact: On an installed system, first-boot generation of /etc/brlapi.key would fail, which matters to BRLTTY users: the archive correctly ships no key (finalisation removes per-device secrets) and the installed system is supposed to mint one. Installed-system qualification stage 10 tests exactly this behaviour and will fail until the program is installed.
gaps.notFixedHere: The one-line fix is to install-root.py, which build/Containerfile copies into the image context: it changes the artifact, supersedes reproducibility qualification target 225a5e1, and requires a fresh local gate and three-builder run. That re-qualification belongs to the installed-system branch, where the root-filesystem-change rule governs it, not to the integration of the already-verified archive evidence.
